question.:question/problem: Simplify the trigonometric expression $\sin \theta(4\cos \theta-6\sin \theta)+\cos \theta(3\sin \theta-6\cos \theta).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
\sin \theta(4\cos \theta-6\sin \theta)+\cos \theta(3\sin \theta-6\cos \theta) = 4\sin \theta\cos \theta-6\sin^{2}\theta+3\sin \theta\cos \theta-6\cos^{2}\theta
$$

Next, we group the $\sin^2 \theta$ and $\cos^2 \theta$ terms.

$$
4\sin \theta\cos \theta-6\sin^{2}\theta+3\sin \theta\cos \theta-6\cos^{2}\theta = 7\sin \theta\cos \theta-6(\sin^{2}\theta+\cos^{2}\theta)
$$

Then, we use $\sin^2{\theta}+\cos^2{\theta}=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
7\sin \theta\cos \theta-6(\sin^{2}\theta+\cos^{2}\theta) = 7 \sin \theta \cos \theta - 6
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\sin \theta(4\cos \theta-6\sin \theta)+\cos \theta(3\sin \theta-6\cos \theta) = 7 \sin \theta \cos \theta - 6.
$$
